sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Kettlebell Carry is a loaded carry exercise that builds full-body strength, endurance, and core stability.

The lifter walks while carrying a kettlebell either at chest height or by their side, maintaining an upright posture throughout the walk.

Loaded carries are highly transferable to real-world strength and reinforce trunk stiffness, grip strength, and conditioning.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Builds anti-flexion and anti-rotation core strength
- Develops grip strength and forearm endurance
- Improves shoulder stability and posture
- Increases conditioning and work capacity
- Reinforces upright bracing patterns
- Highly scalable through load and distance
- Transfers well to everyday lifting and carrying

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Core (Rectus Abdominis, Obliques), Trapezius, Forearms

Secondary: Quadriceps, Glutes, Calves, Shoulders, Upper Back

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Select a kettlebell of appropriate weight.
2. Stand with your feet hip-width apart over the kettlebell.
3. Bend your knees slightly and lift the kettlebell using both hands with a firm grip, keeping your back straight and core engaged.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Lift the kettlebell to chest height, holding it close to your body with elbows tucked in.
2. Alternatively, hold the kettlebell in one hand by your side, switching hands halfway through the walk.
3. Brace your core and keep your shoulders pulled back and down.

sections.heading: Walk With Control
sections.content:
1. Begin walking forward in a controlled manner.
2. Maintain an upright posture with your shoulders back and down.
3. Keep your eyes looking straight ahead and breathe steadily.

sections.heading: Finish the Carry
sections.content:
1. Walk a predetermined distance or for a set period of time.
2. Carefully lower the kettlebell to the ground using your legs to assist.
3. Avoid jerky movements or bending improperly at the waist when setting it down.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Allowing the lower back to round under load
- Letting the shoulders shrug or roll forward
- Leaning to one side during a single-arm carry
- Holding the breath instead of breathing steadily
- Walking with rushed, choppy steps
- Using a load too heavy to maintain posture
- Setting the kettlebell down with poor mechanics

sections.heading: Equipment Required
sections.content:
- Kettlebell of appropriate weight
- Open walking space
- Optional measuring tape or distance markers

sections.heading: Body Position
sections.content:
1. Feet hip-width apart at the start.
2. Core braced, ribs stacked over hips.
3. Shoulders back and down throughout the walk.

sections.heading: Movement Setup
sections.content:
1. Pick up the kettlebell with a hinge pattern.
2. Bring it into the carry position before stepping off.
3. Walk in a straight line with controlled steps.

sections.heading: Safety Considerations
sections.content:
- Keep the path clear of obstacles
- Stop if posture deteriorates
- Use a load you can carry without leaning
- Lower the kettlebell with bent knees, not a rounded back
- Stop immediately if you feel sharp back or shoulder pain
